primitives.name: UTC-Hour Derived Shard Index
primitives.verbatim_quote: ## The fix Derive the shard from the UTC hour rather than a constant: ```ts return { n: new Date(startedAtMs).getUTCHours() % SHARD_COUNT, total: SHARD_COUNT }; ``` UTC because the schedule is a UTC cron expression.

primitives.name: Fixed-Shard Overwrite Regime
primitives.verbatim_quote: ## The bug it fixes, measured ``` [cron:signal-ledger-write] shard=0/1 candidates=118402 written=80000 skipped=0 batches=160 errors=1 ``` **80,000 of 118,402 rows — 67.6% — on every tick.** The route ran a constant `0/1` shard, so each hourly run rewrote the same leading rows and **never reached the tail**.

primitives.assumptions: Constant shard index causes deterministic overwrite behavior.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Failure occurs when shard index does not vary with time.

layer2.mapping: The fixed shard regime mirrors a deadlock condition where data access is monopolized by one logical partition.
layer2.telemetry: Observed 67.6% write failure rate on repeated cron ticks.

The core issue stems from a temporal misalignment between scheduled execution and data partitioning logic. Initially, a fixed shard index (0/1) caused each hourly cron job to repeatedly process only the first portion of the dataset, leaving the remainder untouched. This resulted in a persistent write failure regime where 67.6% of rows were skipped. The root cause lies in the static nature of the shard assignment, which did not evolve with time. By deriving the shard index from the UTC hour modulo shard count, the system now ensures that each hour's execution accesses a different subset of data, thereby enabling full coverage. This transformation maps to a temporal permutation kernel within a distributed processing framework, where the shard index becomes a dynamic function of time rather than a constant. The mathematical formulation \mathcal{S}(t) = \left\lfloor \frac{\text{UTCHour}(t)}{N_{\text{shards}}} \right\rfloor \mod N_{\text{shards}} captures this evolution. The failure mode is thus characterized by a fixed-point attractor in the shard space, while the fix introduces a periodic orbit that spans all partitions over time.
